_comment: Faz 17.1 fake KC realm — NOT_FOR_PROD. Mac dev k3d-dev cluster seed. Faz 23.6 PR-2: subscriberId protocol mapper added (Codex thread `019e03de` AGREE iter-1 model C — built-in oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper, not custom SPI).

users._attribute_comment: Faz 23.6 PR-2 (Codex thread `019e03de` REVISE iter-2 absorb): subscriberId attribute now mirrors the actual user-service `users.id` row that bootstrap/local-fixtures/postgres/seed-dev.sql writes for this email — UUID, not numeric. The backend SubscriberIdentityGuard accepts the claim as a string, so UUID is wire-compatible. Numeric IDs are used in environments where user-service uses bigint primary keys; the realm fixture follows whatever the canonical seed actually inserts.

users._user_comment: Faz 23.6 PR-2: dedicated test persona for the validate-subscriber-id-claim.sh dry-run script. NEVER set this user's password to the operator's login password — see global HARD RULE 'Kullanıcı Aktif Credential'ına Dokunma'. Use scripts/keycloak/validate-subscriber-id-claim.sh and pass EXPECTED_SUBSCRIBER_ID=1204 for a clean check.

clients.name: Platform API Gateway (dev)
clients._protocolMappers_comment: Faz 23.6 PR-2 (Codex thread `019e03de` AGREE iter-1): subscriberId mapper inlined on the gateway client so direct-access-grant tokens (the dry-run validator's path) carry the claim. Prod/test realms should hoist this into a dedicated `canonical-subscriber-id` client scope and add it as a default scope on user-facing clients; for the dev fixture the inline shape keeps the seed file flat and easy to read.

clients.name: Platform Frontend MFE (dev)
clients._protocolMappers_comment: Faz 23.6 PR-2: same subscriberId mapper on the public frontend client so browser tokens (auth code + PKCE) also carry the canonical claim. Without this the SPA would still get tokens missing the claim and the strict-cutover backend flip would 403 every browser session.
